title: HTML Images
summary: Embed images with img, write useful alt text, reserve space with width and height, add captions with figure, and serve responsive images with srcset.
introduction: Images are the heaviest part of most pages and the part most often done badly: missing alt text, layouts that jump while images load, huge photos sent to small phones. This lesson covers the `` element and its attributes, captions with `
learningObjectives: Embed an image with the correct src, alt, width and height
Write alt text for informative and decorative images
Serve responsive images and lazy-load images below the fold

blocks.text: `` is an empty element with two required attributes: `src`, the image location, and `alt`, a text alternative. `width` and `height` give the image's natural size in pixels so the browser can reserve the space before the file arrives.

blocks.title: Layout shift
blocks.text: Without `width` and `height`, the page renders with zero space for the image and then jumps when it loads. That jump is measured by Google as Cumulative Layout Shift and hurts both users and rankings. Always include both attributes; CSS can still scale the image.
`alt` is read aloud by screen readers, shown when the image fails to load and used by search engines. Describe what the image conveys in context, not what it looks like in isolation.

rows: Says what a buyer needs to know
Empty alt tells screen readers to skip it

blocks.text: Never omit `alt` entirely. A missing attribute makes screen readers announce the file name ("IMG underscore 2048 dot jpg"). If the image is decorative, write `alt=""` explicitly.
When an image needs a visible caption, wrap it in `<figure>` and put the caption in `<figcaption>`. The caption is for everyone; the `alt` text is still needed for people who cannot see the image.

A 2000-pixel photo is wasted on a 360-pixel phone screen. `srcset` lists several versions of the image with their widths, and `sizes` tells the browser how wide the image will be displayed, so it can pick the smallest file that still looks sharp.

items: `srcset` = the candidate files and their real pixel widths (`400w`).
`sizes` = how wide the image is rendered: full viewport width on screens up to 600px, otherwise 800px.
`src` = the fallback for very old browsers.

blocks.text: Use `<picture>` when you want different crops per screen size or want to offer a modern format with a fallback:

`loading="lazy"` tells the browser to download an image only when it is about to scroll into view. Use it for images below the first screen, never for the main hero image, which should load as early as possible.

rows: Photos and graphics on the modern web
Much smaller than JPEG at the same quality; use `<picture>` for fallbacks
Vector, scales to any size, tiny file
256 colours; prefer video or animated WebP

blocks.title: Quick checklist
blocks.text: Every image: `src`, meaningful `alt` (or `alt=""`), `width`, `height`. Below the fold: `loading="lazy"`. Large photos: `srcset` and `sizes`.
